summary: Auriga Insights: multipath ACK-deadline cascade causing stream reassembly failures and customer SLA exposure
description:
Issue summary:
During a customer-facing incident window on 2026-03-10 02:12–03:40 UTC, Auriga Insights experienced repeat streaming disconnects and partial transcript reassembly failures. Root trigger: a cascade of ACK-deadline expiries in the streaming-proxy triggered request fanout retries that interleaved partial chunks across multipath sessions, resulting in incomplete transcripts and duplicate token billing.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat sessions frequently encountered truncated or interleaved responses; some sessions reported duplicate final completions.
- Estimated billing exposure for Auriga: ~1.6M tokens billed as duplicates during the 88-minute window.
- SLA risk: customer reported sustained 200s P95 for streaming sessions and threatened executive escalation.

Environment:
- prod/us-east serving fleet behind streaming-proxy revision v2026-03-07-2.
- Dedicated enterprise plan with pinned model redwood-rlhf-v1.

Steps to reproduce (internal reproduction):
1) Send sustained fanout request set (N=40) with long prefix (2k tokens) to streaming endpoint via the streaming-proxy with artificially delayed ACKs.
2) Observe proxy ACK deadline expiries followed by client-side reconnects and multipath session reattachment.
3) Capture reassembly logs and streaming chunk indices to reproduce interleaved sequence numbers.

Observed behavior:
- streaming-proxy missed ACK window for several multiplexed streams, triggered retries that resumed older KV offsets, producing out-of-order chunk sequences.
- Serving runtime accepted resumed sessions without prefix isolation, causing partial KV cache reuse between sessions.
- Customers saw truncated transcripts and duplicate completions on reconnect.

Logs and artifacts:
- Proxy logs: streaming-proxy/errors/ack_deadline_expiry.log (attached).
- Serving runtime traces: traces/2026-03-10/us-east/session-reassembly-*.zip (attachments in linked incident).
- Billing delta snapshot: billing/deltas/auriga-20260310-02-04.csv.

Timeline (high level):
- 02:12 UTC: First ACK-deadline expiry alerts from streaming-proxy (pager).
- 02:20 UTC: Support triage — customer impact confirmed; ticket escalated to SRE.
- 02:28 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied (proxy backoff tightened, retries disabled for multiplexed sessions).
- 02:40 UTC: Full rollback of streaming-proxy revision to v2026-02-25 stable; reassembly success rate restored.
- 03:10 UTC: Billing safe-mode enabled for Auriga (suppress duplicate token billing until reconciliation).
- 03:40 UTC: Incident declared contained; post-incident follow-up planning started.

Customer communication summary:
- Initial acknowledgement sent at 02:24 UTC.
- Status updates at 02:35, 03:05, and 03:50 UTC.
- Dedicated account team call scheduled for 2026-03-11 16:00 UTC to review remediation and credits.
comments: Support (Maya): 2026-03-10 02:25 UTC — Confirmed multiple truncated transcripts and duplicates for three identified customer sessions. Raised severity to P0 and paged SRE.

SRE (Connor): 2026-03-10 02:32 UTC — Observed ACK deadline expiries at the proxy layer correlated with a recent proxy config change. Rolling back proxy revision for affected pool as immediate mitigation.
Customer (Auriga PM - Elena Voss): 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC — Provided sample session IDs and flagged urgent need for billing credits if duplicates are confirmed.
SRE (Connor): 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC — Reassembly success improved after rollback; still seeing isolated KV-offset reuse on resumed sessions. Added audit hooks and blocked retries for resume flows.
Support (Maya): 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC — Enabled billing safe-mode and notified finance. Created follow-up action items for reconciliation and crediting.
Engineering (Amira Chen): 2026-03-11 09:10 UTC — Proposed durable fix: enforce prefix-isolation on resumed sessions and add strict sequence verification before accepting resumed chunks (PR linked).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: a streaming-proxy config change (extended retry window) allowed retries for resumed multiplexed sessions. Retries could reattach stale sequence offsets; without prefix isolation, serving runtime accepted resumed KV pointers, causing chunk interleaving. Confirmed by correlating proxy ack_deadline events with session reassembly traces and duplicate token accounting in billing snapshot.
resolution_notes:
Short-term: rolled back streaming-proxy revision, disabled resume retries for multiplexed sessions, enabled billing safe-mode for Auriga.
Medium-term: landed PR to enforce prefix isolation and sequence validation on session resume (runtime PR #4821).
Follow-up actions: (1) reconcile duplicate-billing exposure with finance and issue customer credit; (2) add automated canary for resume flows that validates sequence monotonicity; (3) update runbook to include immediate proxy rollback path and billing-safe-mode checklist.
Status: Code fix merged and scheduled for staged rollout; reconciliation plan in motion; customer scheduled steering call.
